TRIBUTES TO MARTYRS BHAGAT SINGH, RAJ GURU AND 
SUKHDEV 
MR CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you are aware, today is the 
anniversary of the martyrdom of revolutionaries Bhagat Singh, Raj Guru and 
Sukhdev who laid down their lives at the gallows on this day, seventy years 
ago. Their patriotism, selfless devotion to the cause of the motherland, their 
fearlessness and self-sacrifice has made them national icons. Their last 
thoughts and words were for their country and their wish to see it 
independent of foreign domination. Their words,

देखना है जोर िकतना बाजुए काितल मȂ हȅ। 
still ring in our ears. The Nation can never forget their sacrifice nor repay the 
debt. Today, more than ever before, we need to remember them and others 
like them and be inspired by their ex ample. Hon. Members, let us pay our 
humble tributes to all those great souls who sacrificed their all so that India 
could attain freedom. We pledge ourselves to uphold the cherished values for 
which they laid down their lives. 
I would now request the Members to rise in their places and 
observe silence as a mark of respect in memory of the martyrs.

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
AIDS Education Programme 
† *402. DR. A. K. PATEL: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government plan to start AIDS Education Programme in 
all the Government and semi-Government schools in States, with a view to 
alert the youth, especially the students, against the growing dangers of AIDS; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(DR. C. P. THAKUR): (a) to (c) The Government has already started the 
School AIDS Education Programme. 
It is aimed to cover all the schools in the country during the 
5 years of National AIDS Control Programme (NACP) Phase-ll. A phasing of 
coverage has been envisaged. These programmes are being implemented by 
the respective State AIDS Control Societies in a phased manner. 
Priority is being given to include all higher secondary schools by 
secondary schools. Private and tribal sc hools are also being included in the 
plan. 
It is envisaged that at the end of five years, all the Government 
schools in the States/UTs would be covered. 
Schools AIDS Education Programme addresses students of classes IX & 
XI and focuses on raising awareness levels, helping young people resist peer 
pressure and developing a safe and responsible lifestyle. The programme 
reinforces family values and respect for the opposite sex. The activities 
include training of teachers and peer ed ucators among students , role playing, 
debates and discussions, question box and access to referral services, if 
necessary.

AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:

(a) whether it is a fact that M/s Ranbaxy, Cadila Health Care and Torrent 
were granted permission to market Sildenafil Citrate, a Vigara substitute, on 9th 
January, 2001, and the formulation was available on 10th January throughout 
the country; 
(b) if so, how these companies manufactured formulation of sildenafil

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
Clearance of Clopidogril 
*406. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN: 
SHRI VIJAY SINGH YADAV: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) what is the time taken for granting approval for new drugs; 
(b) whether it is a fact that Clopidogril, a new drug, was approved by 
DCGI within three days of submission of clinical trials; 
(c) if so, whether the DCGI office ap proves all new drugs in such a 
short-time; and 
(d) the names of new drugs cleared during 2000 and the time taken to 
grant first approval, after submission of clinical trial reports for each drug? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. C.P. 
THAKUR): (a) to (d) The time taken for evaluation of new drug applications 
varies according to the nature of the molecule/ drug. Evaluation of a new drug 
application is a complex process and the details are spelt out in Scheduled Y of 
the Drug and Cosmetic Rules, 1945. The modalities involved would inter-alia 
include initial evaluation by experts of chemical and physical characteristics, animal 
toxicity, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the drug, approval of 
protocols for clinical trials as well as data generated by the various clinical 
trials, results of testing of the new drug by the Central Government Drug lab, 
etc. 
Therefore, depending upon the nature of the application, it may normally 
take more than 5 years for approval of investigational new drug (A drug molecule 
not tested on human beings anywhere in the world), about 1—3 years for the 
first time approval of the drug already approved elsewhere and about 2-3 
months for subsequent applications for already approved drugs. This is, 
however, subject to submission of all required data as per provisions of 
Schedule Y of Drug and Cosmetic Rules. In the case of certain critical drugs, 
which have been already approved elsewhere in developed countries, and 
10 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
which are of importance from the point of view of Public Health, clearance is 
also given on a fast track basis without doing local clinical trials. 
The application from M/s Torrent Pharmaceuticals Ltd. for approval of 
Clopidogril was received on 5.7.2000. Th is was a drug already approved 
abroad. Permission to undertake phase-Ill clinical trials and tab testing for 
quality from the Central Government laboratory, Kolkota, was given on 
3.10.2000. The report from Central Drug Laboratory declaring the drug as of 
standard quality was received on 4.12.200 0. The data from the clinical trials 
was received on 5.1.2001. After evaluating the data, the drug was approved 
on 1.2.2001. Hence the concern that approval for Clopidogril was given 
within three days of submission of clinical trials is not factually correct. 
Details of New Drugs cleared during the year 2000, alongwith date of 
first approval granted and date of submission of report on clinical trials, is 
given in the Statement. (See below) The time taken between date of approval 
and receipt of the report on  clinical trials varies since data relating to quality 
is also subject to receipt of data re garding Quality Control from the Central 
Drug labs.

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
Closure of B ha rat Gold Mines 
*407. DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: Will the Minister of MINES be 
pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred Question 945, given in the Rajya 
Sabha on the 2nd March, 2000, and state: 
(a) whether 120 old mines of Bharat Gold Mines Limited, Kolar, 
Karnataka, would be closed down from 31st March, 2001; 
(b) whether the employees have been asked to give option under 
Voluntary Separation Scheme by 9th February, 2001; 
(c) whether the Scheme would benefit the employees; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF MINES (SHRI SUNDAR LAL PATWA): (a) Board 
for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) after considering the 
matter for eight years passed final orders on 12.6.2000 concluding that it is 
just and equitable that Bharat Gold Mines Limited (BGML) be would up 
under Section 20(1) of SICA, 1985 and forwarded its opinion to the Registrar 
of High Court of Karnataka on 30.6.2000. Besides this. Ministry of Labour, 
Government of India, accorded permission for closure of BGML w.e.f. 
1.3.2001 under Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 vide their order dated 
29.1.2001. The Employee Union of BGML moved High Court of Karnataka 
against the orders of BIFR and that of Ministry of Labour. The single judge 
bench of High Court of Karnataka has passed orders on 16.3.2001 quashing 
the BIFR orders dated 12.6.2000 and Ministry of Labour order dated 
29.1.2000. 
(b) Voluntary Separation Scheme (VSS) was thrown open w.e.f. 
11.12.2000 for one month allowing employees either to opt for Heavy 
Industries  package or Gujarat  package.   However,  High  Court of 
Karnataka extended the last date for opting VSS upto 28.2.2001. 
(c) and (d) Under Heavy Industry package an employee is entitled 
to get ex-gratia payment equivalent to 1-V 2 month's emoluments (pay 
+ DA) for each completed year of service or the monthly emolument 
at the time of retirement multiplied by the balance months of service 
left before normal date of retirement, whichever is less. However, all 
14 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
those who have completed not less than 30  years of service, will be eligible 
for a maximum of 60 months of salary/wage as compensation. This will be 
subject to the amount, not exceeding th e salary/wage for the balance period 
of service left (at the rate of monthly salary/wage at the time of voluntary 
retirement). Under Gujarat package an employee is entitled to get 
compensation consisting of salary of 35 days for every completed year 
service and 25 days for the balance of service left until superannuation. The 
compensation will be subject to a minimum of Rs. 25000 or 250 days salary 
whichever is higher. However, this compensation shall not exceed the sum of 
the salary that the employee would draw at the prevailing level for the 
balance of the period left before superannuation. Salary for purpose of VRS 
will consist of basic pay and DA only. Ar rears of wages due to revision etc. 
will not be included in computing th e eligible amount. Payment of bonus 
should conform to the provisions in the Bonus Act. Casual leave may be 
encashed in proportionate measure upto the date of VRS. Under these 
packages in addition to ex-gratia/compensation, notice pay, leave salary, TA 
for settling etc. are also given.

*412. SHRI PRAKANTA WARISA: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred 
Question 293, given in the Rajya Sabha on the 23rd February, 2001 and state: 
(a) the details of literacy rate among tribal and hilly people, STs, SCs and 
women in Assam; and 
(b) the details of steps taken by Government to remove illiteracy from the 
State? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) and (b) The literacy rate of Scheduled 
Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Women in the State of Assam was 53.94%, 
49.16% and 43.03% respectively, as per 1991 Census.  As  per  the  NSSO  
53rd  Round  Survey  (1997)  the  male 
24 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
literacy rate was 82% while the female literacy rate was 66% in the State. 
Latest figures on literacy rate among the SCs, STs and Women will be 
available on the publication of 2001 Census Report. 
The Government has taken following steps;—  
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan 
A new Scheme of "Sarva Shiksha A bhiyan" incorporating all existing 
Schemes and Programmes in Elemen tary Education Sector has been 
launched. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is a holistic and convergent 
approach to implement Universalisa tion of Elementary Education in a 
mission mode with a clear district focus. The goals of SSA are as follows: 
i) All 6 — 14 age children in schools/EGS centre/bridge course  
by 2003, 
ii) AH   6   —   14   age   children   complete   five   year   primary 
education by 2007 and 
iii) All 6 — 14 age children complete eight years of schooling by  
2010. 
The approach is community-owned and village education plans prepared 
in consultation with Panchayati Raj Institutions will form the basis of district 
elementary education plans. Funds to  States would be channelised to 
registered societies at State level. Th ere will be a focus on districts having 
low female literacy among Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The 
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan will cover the entire country with a special focus on 
educational needs of girls, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and other 
children in difficult circumstances. 
Efforts would be made to give priority to the 148 districts where the 
female literacy among SC/ST was less than 10 per cent in 1991. Many of 
these have been covered under the DPEP or the Lok Jumbish project in 
Rajasthan. The uncovered districts would be selected first and in the DPEP 
districts already covered, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan will consider proposals for 
vertical extension of th e Project to cover the Upper Primary Section. 
Proposals for upgradation of primary and upper primary schools in Low 
Female 
25 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
Literacy Blocks, provision for teacher  recruitment and incentive schemes, 
would also be considered. The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan shall accord the highest 
priority to community monitoring, transparency in programme planning and 
implementation capacity building at all levels and adoption of a mission 
approach by the mainstream Education Department functionaries to achieve 
UEE in a given time frame. There will be special focus on girl children 
belonging to SC/ ST communities, urban slums dwellers and low female 
literacy blocks. 
This Ministry have released grants amounting to Rs.22.27 crore to 21 
States/UTs for starting preparatory activities in 134 districts. Four districts 
viz. Dhemaji, Karimganj, Nalbari and Ti nsukia in Assam have been covered 
under SSA. A grant of Rs. 74,00,000/- has been sanctioned for starting pre-
project activities in these districts. 
National Literacy Mission 
National Literacy Mission seeks to attain full literacy i.e. sustainable 
threshold level of 75 per-cent literacy by 2005. It seeks to achieve this goal by 
imparting functional literacy to non-literate in 15-39 age group. 
Major thrust of programmes of National Literacy Mission is on promotion 
of literacy among women, members belonging to SCs and STs particularly in 
rural areas. 
The strategy adopted is imparting basic literacy through Total Literacy 
Campaigns followed by Post Literacy by consolidation and moving Continuing 
Education for life-long learning and creation of a learning society. 
The funding ratio between the Centre and State Governments for normal 
districts is 2:1, whereas for districts under Tribal Sub-Plan the ratio is 4:1. 
Annual plan provision in 2000-2001 was Rs. 120 crore and it has now been 
stepped up to Rs. 200 crore in budget proposals of 2001-2002. 
Steps taken to give greater thrust to remove illiteracy include revision of 
National Literacy Mission (NLM) parameters and enhancement of financial 
norms integration of the phases of Total 
26 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
Literacy and Post Literacy, delegation  of powers to State Literacy Mission 
Authorities, enlarging the scope of Continuing Education, strengthening of Jan 
Shikshan Sansthans and extending their activities in rural areas, revitalizing State 
Resource Centres for preparation of better teaching learning materials and 
improved quality of training. 
All the 23 districts in Assam have been covered under Total Literacy 
Campaign out of them 10 districts are in Post Literacy Programmes. 
District Primary Education Programme 
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of District Primary Education Programme 
(DPEP), which aims to achieve universal primary education, is being 
implemented in nine districts out of 23 districts in Assam through a State Society viz 
Assam Prathamik Siksba Achani Parishad, Guwahati. These nine districts which 
had female literacy rate less than th e national average of 38.3 per cent are 
predominantly rural in character. DPEP is under implementation in 4 
districts—Darrang, Dhubri, Morigoan and Karbi Anglong under Phase I since 
1994 and in 5 districts—Barpet, Bongaigaon, Goalpara, Kokrajhar and Sonitpur 
under Phase II since 1996. The total project outlay of DPEP in Assam is Rs. 285.85 
crore. The first phase of the programme will expire in March, 2002 and second 
phase in June, 2003. The grant-in-aid released by the GOI to the above mentioned

In order to make available fertilizers at affordable prices, the Government 
provides subsidy on urea and concession on de-controlled Potassic and

Experts under the Chairmanship of Dr. Y.K. Alagh to address to the total

THE   MINISTER   OF   STATE   IN   THE   MINISTRY   OF

51

No such tests have been carried out on commonly used drugs for cold and 
cough to assess the level of risk involved in drugs containing certain 
chemicals. 
However, a drug named Phenylpropanolamine (PPA), an ingredient 
used in cough and cold preparations as decongestant has been assessed in 
United States of America for a reported linkage with increasing risk of 
haemorrhagic strokes in women. PPA is also used in weight loss preparation 
in USA. Based on the study report, FDA, USA advised consumers to stop 
taking drug products containing PPA and declared its withdrawal from the 
US market. 
Since in India, PPA is used only in many cold and cough formulations, 
the position has been reviewed by the Expert Committee of the DTAB. This 
Committee concluded that the eviden ce of a link between haemorrhagic 
stroke and PPA is weak and is mainly associated with uses which are not yet 
licensed in the country a view similar to  that of the Medical Control Agency, 
U.K. Therefore, the DTAB has recommended that syrup formulations 
containing PPA as an ingredient should not contain more than 12.5 mg/dose 
of PPA and tablets should not have more than 25 mg of PPA/tablet. It has 
also recommended that the daily dose should not be more than 50 mg for 
children and 100 mg for adults. Instructions in this regard are being circulated 
to all State Licensing Authorities to monitor its sale in the country.

† 3021. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN': 
SHRI* RAM JETHMALANI;

(b) if so, what are the facts in this regard;  
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
52 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) whether Government have made any efforts to find out the production cost 
of chemical fertilizers in America, Canada, Brazil, Australia and other countries; 
and 
(d) if so, the details of production cost in those countries and to what 
extent it is higher in India? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI SATYA BRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) and (b) The 
production cost of chemical fertilizers in the country is currently higher than 
the international price. The reason fo r higher cost is mainly on account of 
higher feedstock/raw material cost in  India. In the case of nitrogenous 
fertilizers, plants in the exporting co untries are generally based on natural 
gas. As per available information, the cost of natural gas in those countries is 
around US$ 1 per million BTU or less, whereas in India as against the 
delivered cost is US $ 2.33 to 2.39 for the plants based on land fall point and 
US $ 2.76 to 3.07 for the plants based on HBJ pipeline. The feedstock cost of 
the plants based on naphtha and fuel oil is still higher. The delivered cost of 
naphtha at the factory gate is US $ 7.68 to 9.16 and that of fuel oil is US $ 5.59 
to 6.31 per million BTU. 
In regard to phosphatic fertilizers, plants in India are mostly dependent on 
imported intermediates or raw materials, the landed cost of which per tonne of 
DAP is usually higher than the landed cost of DAP itself. In addition, the industry 
has to incur conversion and capital related costs. 
(c) and (d) It is difficult to get the production cost of chemical fertilizers in 
other countries, which is generally kept confidential for commercial interests.

3033. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS be pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred Question 863, given in 
the Rajya Sabha on the 2nd March, 2001 and state: 
(a) whether wildlife mafias are having sophisticated weapons and the 
protectors are deprived of such facilities;

(c) whether Government propose to take over the responsibility, at 
their own, to protect forest areas in the country and if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) to (c) The lucrative nature of illegal wildlife trade and the high 
price offered to various wildlife pro ducts has led to creation of wildlife 
mafias equipped with all modem amenities. 
The strategies for effective protec tion of wildlife and forests were 
discussed at the Conference of State Forests and Environment Ministers held 
on 29th to 31st January, 2001 at Coimbatore. A Coimbatore Charter was 
unanimously adopted with the following strategies:—  
(i) The ban on recruitment of forestry personnel shall be lifted and the 
vacancies filled up immediately on the lines of Police Department. The 
field formations shall the reorganized into viable units and be 
provided with adequate mobility, fire arms and effective 
communication network. 
(ii) An effective mechanism for intelligence gathering and data base of 
habitual offenders should be developed for preventing wildlife crimes. 
(iii) Create effective enforcement infra structure such as roads, buildings, 
wireless, equipments, vehicles, arms etc. for the protection of forests 
and Protected Areas. 
(iv)   Adequate   expertise   shall   be   developed   for   prosecuting 
69 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
offenders    and    training    be    organized    for    undertaking 
investigations. 
(v) Steps shall be taken immediately for designating special courts 
for wildlife offences. 
(vi) Wild animals do considerable damage to agricultural crops in 
areas adjoining national parks and sanctuaries, causing considerable 
concern, thereby requiring formulation of an appropriate insurance 
scheme for compensating damage to agricultural crops falling within 
five kilometers of national parks and sanctuaries. 
(vii) Existing provisions for payment of compensation in the cases 
of deaths due to wild animals were  emphasized, with the objective of 
ensuring compliance by the State/Union Territories Governments.

GMPs have been stipulated as a statutory requirement under the

Testing* for Packaged Drinking Water 
3050. SHRI KULDIP NAYYAR: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for new notification on packaged drinking water, making it 
compulsory to have an elaborate laboratory test and the reasons for so many tests 
to be carried out; 
(b) whether this kind of testing is also required for fruit juices or soft drinks 
and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) whether this is an anti small-scale and pro-multination.u act, because the 
small scale industry cannot afford these expenses? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) Due to the rapid growth of the 
packaged drinking water industry in the large as well as small scale sectors and the 
reports of sale of spurious quality packaged water, the need was felt to specify 
standards and guidelines to regulate the quality of these products and their 
manufacture. 
Therefore, the Government have notified the standards of packaged 
drinking water vide Gazette Notification dated 29.09.2000 (effective from 
29.03.2001) which require mandatory certification by Bureau of Indian Standards 
(BIS) This notification was issued after 
89 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
notifying the draft rules calling for public comments, based on the 
recommendations of the Central Committee for Food Standards (CCFS), and 
after holding wide consultations with all concerned Departments/Ministries and 
expert institutions. 
Since this is an item of mass consumption, the process of enforcing 
quality control would require testing samples of packaged drinking water for all the 
chemical and microbiological parameters prescribed in the standards for this product 
which are felt necessary from the point of view of health. 
(b) Fruit Juices and Soft Drinks are not under compulsory certification 
scheme of BIS. These are also covered under Fruit Products Order 1955, 
under which licenses are given to these products after sanitary conditions of the 
manufacturing units are checked. The routine checking of Fruit Juices and Soft 
Drinks is also carried out regularly under PFA Act, 1954 to ensure compliance with 
the parameters specified in the standards for these products. 
(c) No, Sir. There is no separate provision for certification etc. for large 
scale or small scale units. The fixation of rate of marking fee by Bureau of Indian 
Standards is according to the quantum of production. Since the number of 
requirements to be tested for pack aged drinking water are higher, the 
operative cost/testing charges are higher. However, efforts are being made by 
Bureau of Indian Standards to bring down the cost of testing by approving more test 
houses capable of testing the product.

has been prescribed under the PFA Rules since BIS has the powers and the 
facility under the BIS Act 1986 and Rules 1987 (Certification Regulations 1988) 
to certify quality control of food products. This procedure is normally stipulated in 
the case of those products where it is felt necessary for quality of the product to be 
closely monitored. 
(b) The fee for implementing the certification scheme is levied by BIS 
keeping in view the need to maintain continuous surveillance over the 
production centre and product by checking the infrastructure for manufacture 
through periodic visits to the units and by drawing and testing of samples, both 
from the production site as well as from the market. 
(c) BIS has informed that the main basis for fixing the marking is the total 
cost of operation of licence, which is different for large scale and small scale 
units. Based on this a maximum marking fee is fixed. A unit rate is also fixed to 
calculate the marking fee according to the quantum of production where the 
amount chargeable per annum exceeds the minimum, then the total amount is 
charged on unit rate basis. The marking fee is charged primarily to recover the 
operating cost of the license which includes testing samples drawn from the 
factory and market, administrative cost of inspection, supervision etc. Where the 
number of parameters to be tested are high, as in this 
91 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
case, the operative cost also increases proportionately. Efforts are on to bring 
down the cost of testing by approving more test houses (who are capable of 
testing the product) and also developing in house testing facilities which 
would bring down the overall marking fee. 
(d) The amount of marking fee will depend on the number of Industries 
that obtain certification and the quant um of production. Hence an exact 
figure cannot be estimated at this juncture. 
(e) The operation of the Certification Marks Scheme is covered under 
BIS act 1986 Rules 1987 (Certification Regulations 1988) under which the 
Bureau is empowered to charge a fee, (Chapter V, Clause 15(2).) of the BIS 
Act is reproduced below: 
"The grant of renewal of the license under sub-section (1) shall be 
subject to such conditions and on payment of such fees as may be determined 
by regulations."

wise; and 
93 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2001] 
(c) what steps the Central and State Governments have taken to control

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) and (b) Ten Tribal predominant 
districts of Andhra Pradesh have been identified as Malaria hard core districts 
and included in the Enhanced Malaria Control Project (EMCP) with World 
bank Support for intensification of malaria control activities by way of 
additional inputs through a mix of interventions. Malaria incidence and 
deaths due to Malaria in these districts have shown declining trend during the 
year 2000 as compared to 1999. During the year 2000, the number of deaths 
recorded in these districts have been 7 as compared to 10 deaths during the 
year 1999. 
(c) For effective prevention and cont rol of Malaria in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh, the following steps are being taken by the Central as well as 
State Governments:—  
1. Early Detection and Prompt Treatment (EDPT) of cases has been 
intensified by gearing up surveillance. 
2. Facilities for detection and treatment of cases have been extended to 
the village level by involving coummunity volunteers as Drug 
Distribution Center (DDCs) and Malaria Link Volunteers (MLVs) in 
high risk areas. 
3. Rapid diagnostic kits for malaria case detection has been introduced 
for piloting. 
4. Identification of referral centre for the management of severe and 
complicated malaria. 
5. Providing alternative anti-malarials in Chloroquine resistant areas. 
6. Vector control measures have been intensified by prioritization of 
areas for selective spray with appropriate insecticides and alternative 
vector control methods. 
7. Newer   and   more   effective   alternative   insecticides   like 
Synthetic Pyrethroids have been introduced in the programme.

8. Information Education and Communication (IEC) activities for 
Public awareness have been intensified. 
9. Capabilities for Epidemic preparedness and repid response are being

Endosulfan is a broad spectrum orga nochlorine insec ticide/ acaricide

of Agricultural Research, this insecticide is considered to be relatively safe

3105. SHRI KHAGEN DAS: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the drop-out rate of tribal students in 
different States has been increasing for the last three years; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof, year-w ise and State-wise and the action 
being taken to check this trends? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) and (b) No, Sir. The dropout rates 
for tribal students have generally been declining over the last three years. 
Several measures have been taken to reduce drop-out rates among 
Scheduled Tribes particularly at el ementary stage. These include micro-
planning, Community mobilization, improvement of school infrastructure 
through Operation Blackboard Scheme, District Primary Education 
Programme (DPEP), National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary 
Education (Mid-day Meals), various incentive schemes such as scholarships, 
free-ships, free textbooks, uniforms, construction of hostels and residential 
schools for Scheduled Tribes students etc. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan that has 
recently been launched to achieve universalisation of elementary education in 
a holistic and convergent manner has a special focus on disadvantaged groups 
including Scheduled Tribes.

Promotion of Sanskrit 
3120. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY:  Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that a sizeable section of the people 
in the country are keen that Government take active steps to develop and 
propularise Sanskrit, which contains acme of Indian philosophy and wisdom; 
(b) if so, whether Government are thinking of taking effective and 
quick steps in this regard; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. Government has already 
taken several steps to develop and popularize Sanskrit. These include a 
Central Plan Scheme for the development of Sanskrit education   through  the   
State   Governments.   Under  this  scheme 
170 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
financial assistance is given to Sanskrit pandits in indigent circumstances, 
scholarships are provided to Sans krit students, facilities provided for 
teaching Sanskrit in schools, assistance given for the modernization of 
Sanskrit Pathshalas and grants given to State Governments for various 
promotional schemes for Sanskrit. 
In addition, Government has set up the Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan, an 
autonomous organization for the promotion of Sanskrit. It imparts Sanskrit 
studies up to doctorate level in its 8 Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeethas and 21 
Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya/Shodh Sansthans. It also provides financial 
assistance under various other schemes for Sanskrit. 
Further, Government has set up two deemded Sanskrit Universities,   
the   Shri   Lai   Bahadur   Shastri   Rashtriya   Sanskrit 
Vidyapeetha at New Delhi and Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha at Tirupati. 
They provide degree, diploma and Ph.D. courses. 
In  addition,  numerious  Central  and  other  Universities  and 
schools affiliated to the Central Board of Secondary Education offer Sanskrit 
courses. University Grants Commission (UGC) also has a special Assistance 
Programme for Sanskrit. 
Further, various State Governments also have their own schemes for the 
propagation of Sanskrit. 
Recently, the UGC has formulated a Scheme for the promotion of 
Sanskrit. It has decided, in principle, to set up simple Sanskrit speaking 
centres in selected universities so that those interested in Sanskrit are 
benefited. 
Government also honours eminent Sanskrit scholars every year with its 
President's award of the Certificate of Honour.

Investment by IT industry in Technical Education 
3125. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether it is a fact that about Rs, 2000 crores are required for 
technical education, to keep leadership in IT market; 
(b) if so, whether Government would make the IT industry also share this 
investment; 
(c) whether any blueprint has been prepared for this; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (d) The Task Force on HRD in IT in its 
Interim Report has made forty-seven (47) recommendations aimed at ensuring 
supply of adequate and quality IT manpower for both meeting the domestic and 
global demands. This shall be done by strenghtening and upgrading the 
technical education system in the country. These recommendations relate to IT 
faculty development, IT curricula & courseware development, strengthening of 
computing and networking facilities, digitization and modernization of libraries, 
use of IT for administrative support services and promoting interface with 
industry. Investment required would be to the tune of Rs. 2000 crore (central 
share along) over a seven year period (up to the end of 10th Five Year Plan). 
Most of the capital outlay would, however, be required in first 3-4 years only. 
These interventions would result in overall increase in availability of quality IT 
manpower in larger numbers in the country. This will help the Indian software 
services sector to increase its productivity and move up the value chain, 
enabling the country to capture larger share of global markets of IT software 
and services.

(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH): (a) to (0 Long Welded Rails can fracture in

patrolling of track in the early hours of morning. To assist patrolmen in

Discovery of Planets beyond Pluto by Indian Scientists 
3161. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether, as reported in the D eccan Chronicle dated 21st January, 
2001, two Indian Scientists have claimed to have discovered two more planets 
in the Solar System beyond the orbit of Pluto, the ninth Planet; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the claim has been accepte d by the International Science 
Congress if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) what steps are proposed to be taken to provide assistance and 
encourgement to the concerned scientists? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI BACHI SINGH RAW AT): (a) to (d) The Deccan 
Chronicle has reported a claim by two scientists that there exist two more 
planets beyond Pluto. The reported claim is not an observational discovery. It 
is an untested prediction, based on a formula proposed by the authors, not 
generally known in the astronomical community. 
The Titius-Bode law cited by the authors is also an empirical formula 
without as yet, a physical basis. The predicted diameters and masses of the 
proposed planets are large, and as such the planets should have been 
observed already. The authors do not have clear reasons why they are 
unobservable by the modem optical and radio telescopes. In fact, dozens of 
asteriod-like objects beyond the crbits of Pluto and Neptune have been 
detected by astronomers since 1990s, that have much smaller sizes which 
suggest that such planets are not present. The reported claims does not seem to 
have been seriously considered by the astronomical community nor has a 
detailed paper 
206 

[23 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
been published in any standard astronomical journals.  Hence, no steps are 
proposed to be taken to provide assistance at this stage.

Stepping up of an Indo-US Science and Technology Forum 
3163. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: WiU the Minister of SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that India and US have signed an agreement to 
set up an Indo-US Science and Technology forum; 
(b) if so, the main objectives of the forum; and 
(c) how Government Plan to implement these objectives? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE   
AND   TECHNOLOGY    IN   THE   MINISTRY   OF 
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI BACHI SINGH RAW AT): (a) to 
(c) Yes sir. An agreement on the Indo-US Science and Technology Forum 
was signed on March 21, 2000 in New Delhi. The main objectives of the 
Forum are : (1) To facilitate and promote Indo-US interaction of 
governments, academia and industry in Science and Technology and other 
related areas. (2) To focus on issues of common concern and activities of 
mutual benefit while exploring trends in science and technology. (3) To 
promote research and development, the transfer of technology and creation of 
a comprehensive electronic referen ce source for Indo-US Science and 
Technology Cooperation. (4) To promot e an active electronic exchange of 
ideas and opportunities in Indo-US Science and Technology Cooperation. 
The Indo-US Science and Technology Forum has been registered as a 
society under Indian Societies Registration Act XXI of 1860. The Governing 
Body of this society consists of 7 members each nominated by the Indian 
Government and the US Government. The Governing Body is responsible for 
drawing up the plans to implement the objectives of the Indo-US Science and 
Technology Forum.
